title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #6

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A pupil faces the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is on the pupil's right hand? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. East
   C. South
   D. North

2. What does the size of a county mean? (1 mark)
   A. The number of schools in it
   B. The number of roads in it
   C. The number of people in it
   D. The area of land it covers

3. County X covers 8 grid squares and County Y covers 5 grid squares. Which statement is correct? (1 mark)
   A. County X is bigger than County Y
   B. We cannot compare them
   C. County Y is bigger than County X
   D. They are the same size

4. What is a lake? (1 mark)
   A. A dry plain
   B. A very high mountain
   C. A large area of water surrounded by land
   D. A long channel of flowing water

5. Which of these is one of the four seasons in the county? (1 mark)
   A. Spring
   B. Autumn
   C. Rainy season
   D. Winter

6. What is a season? (1 mark)
   A. A type of crop
   B. The weather on one day
   C. A kind of clothing
   D. A part of the year with a typical kind of weather

7. In many parts of Kenya, when do the long rains usually come? (1 mark)
   A. September only
   B. March to May
   C. June to August
   D. January to February

8. What is weather? (1 mark)
   A. How the air is on a particular day
   B. The number of months in a year
   C. The size of a county
   D. The height of a mountain

9. What is a cultural centre? (1 mark)
   A. A place for repairing cars
   B. A bank
   C. A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive
   D. A hospital

10. Which place in Nairobi shows traditional homes and dances of many communities? (1 mark)
   A. Fort Jesus
   B. Lamu Old Town
   C. Bomas of Kenya
   D. Gede Ruins

11. Which of these shows interdependence? (1 mark)
   A. A man refusing help
   B. Farmer sells maize and buys clothes from a tailor
   C. A woman sleeping
   D. A child eating alone

12. What do traders do for farmers? (1 mark)
   A. Grow their crops
   B. Buy their crops and take them to markets
   C. Build their houses
   D. Teach their children

13. In a bar graph of sub-county populations, which sub-county has the tallest bar? (1 mark)
   A. The one with the most people
   B. The one with the fewest people
   C. The largest area
   D. The smallest area

14. Which is a reason why fewer people live in a forest reserve? (1 mark)
   A. It has good roads
   B. It has many towns
   C. People are not allowed to settle there
   D. There are too many houses

15. Which pattern describes each family living far from the next on its own land? (1 mark)
   A. Clustered
   B. Linear
   C. Crowded
   D. Scattered

16. Which houses in Lamu were built with coral stone? (1 mark)
   A. Round grass houses
   B. Old town houses
   C. Boats
   D. Tents

17. What is a kiondo? (1 mark)
   A. A house
   B. A basket
   C. A shirt
   D. A drum

18. Which practice do Kenyan laws forbid because it harms girls? (1 mark)
   A. Wearing beads
   B. Cooking ugali
   C. Female genital mutilation
   D. Playing bao

19. Why do schools have rules? (1 mark)
   A. To stop friendship
   B. To make pupils sad
   C. To keep everyone safe and help learning
   D. To stop lessons

20. Why do we recite the school motto? (1 mark)
   A. To hide
   B. To scare others
   C. To waste time
   D. To remember what the school stands for

21. Which county is famous for its tea farms? (1 mark)
   A. Lamu
   B. Kericho
   C. Marsabit
   D. Turkana

22. Reduce, reuse and recycle are ways of doing what? (1 mark)
   A. Growing tea
   B. Building roads
   C. Drying fish
   D. Cutting down waste

23. Which activity involves growing crops and keeping animals? (1 mark)
   A. Mining
   B. Tourism
   C. Fishing
   D. Farming

24. What does jua kali mean in Kiswahili? (1 mark)
   A. Rainy day
   B. Big factory
   C. Cold wind
   D. Hot sun

25. Which of these is an honest practice in business? (1 mark)
   A. Giving correct change
   B. Hiding sales money
   C. Selling bad goods as good
   D. Cheating customers

26. Which of these is a viable project? (1 mark)
   A. One that nobody wants
   B. One that is dangerous
   C. One that costs more than it earns
   D. One that people want, is safe and can earn more than it costs

27. Why should every sale be recorded? (1 mark)
   A. So that the project fails
   B. So that pupils have more homework
   C. So that money can be checked and accounted for
   D. So that profit disappears

28. Which action shows cleanliness? (1 mark)
   A. Writing on walls
   B. Spitting in class
   C. Putting litter in the bin
   D. Throwing rubbish on the ground

29. Which is a good way to develop a quality like punctuality? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Wait for others to do it
   C. Practise it once a year
   D. Practise it every day

30. Which action shows responsibility? (1 mark)
   A. Waiting to be told each time
   B. Refusing to help
   C. Breaking things
   D. Doing your class duty without being reminded

31. Why is it important to plan a peace-building activity? (1 mark)
   A. So that it is cancelled
   B. So that nobody joins
   C. So that it runs well and everyone knows what to do
   D. So that it wastes time

32. Which is a way to promote child rights in school? (1 mark)
   A. Hiding problems
   B. Making posters and songs on child protection
   C. Ignoring children with problems
   D. Bullying

33. Which of these can you call for help in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. A bakery
   B. A shop
   C. A cinema
   D. The child helpline 116

34. In an election, 12 pupils voted for Amina and 10 for Brian. Who wins? (1 mark)
   A. Amina
   B. Both
   C. Brian
   D. Nobody

35. What does equality mean in an election? (1 mark)
   A. Only boys vote
   B. Some people have many votes
   C. Only teachers vote
   D. Each person has one vote of equal value

36. Which item usually comes first on an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. Reports
   B. Closing remarks
   C. Suggestions
   D. Opening prayer or song

37. Who usually guides a Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. A driver
   B. A stranger
   C. A teacher patron
   D. A police officer

38. Who leads a sub-location? (1 mark)
   A. Assistant chief
   B. Governor
   C. Speaker
   D. President

39. What do village elders do? (1 mark)
   A. Teach maths only
   B. Welcome visitors and help settle small quarrels
   C. Fly aeroplanes
   D. Make cars

40. Who is the head of the national government? (1 mark)
   A. The Speaker
   B. The Governor
   C. The MCA
   D. The President

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain why a Children's Government should not punish pupils. (3 marks)

42. Describe how you would draw a sketch map of your county in five steps. (5 marks)

43. Write a short motto and explain what it asks pupils to do. (3 marks)

44. Give three benefits of industries to a county. (3 marks)

45. Name the six aspects of traditional culture. (3 marks)

46. Who is the patron of a Children's Government? (2 marks)

47. Explain the meaning of a good citizen in school. (2 marks)

48. Name two landforms and two water features. (4 marks)

49. Name the four in-between points on a compass and say between which cardinal points each lies. (4 marks)

50. Describe how to draw a dot map showing population distribution in your county. (4 marks)

51. Explain why it is important to keep records of income and costs. (3 marks)

52. State three duties of the governor. (3 marks)

53. County A covers 15 grid squares and County B covers 9 grid squares. Which is larger and by how many squares? Show your working. (3 marks)

54. Describe two peace-building activities that a school can carry out. (4 marks)

55. Explain three rules of good digital citizenship. (3 marks)

56. Describe how a class can invite a resource person to talk about leadership. (4 marks)

57. Name the four cardinal points. (2 marks)

58. Explain why children with special needs need extra care and respect. (3 marks)

59. Give two ways in which Mount Kenya is useful. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — South
   Facing east, south is on the right hand.

2. D — The area of land it covers
   Size means the area of land, not the population.

3. A — County X is bigger than County Y
   8 squares is more land than 5 squares.

4. C — A large area of water surrounded by land
   A lake has land all around it.

5. C — Rainy season
   The four seasons are hot, cold, dry and rainy.

6. D — A part of the year with a typical kind of weather
   A season is the weather that is typical over several months.

7. B — March to May
   The long rains are usually from March to May.

8. A — How the air is on a particular day
   Weather describes sun, rain, wind and temperature at a given time.

9. C — A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive
   Cultural centres show dances, homes, crafts and foods.

10. C — Bomas of Kenya
   The Bomas of Kenya is a cultural centre in Nairobi.

11. B — Farmer sells maize and buys clothes from a tailor
   The farmer and tailor depend on each other.

12. B — Buy their crops and take them to markets
   Traders buy from farmers and sell in towns.

13. A — The one with the most people
   Taller bars show bigger values.

14. C — People are not allowed to settle there
   Forest reserves are protected.

15. D — Scattered
   Scattered means spread widely apart.

16. B — Old town houses
   Old Lamu houses used coral stone.

17. B — A basket
   The kiondo is a woven basket.

18. C — Female genital mutilation
   FGM is against the law.

19. C — To keep everyone safe and help learning
   Rules protect people and help learning.

20. D — To remember what the school stands for
   Reciting reminds us of the school's aims.

21. B — Kericho
   Kericho is a major tea growing area.

22. D — Cutting down waste
   The three Rs cut down waste.

23. D — Farming
   Farming is growing crops and keeping livestock.

24. D — Hot sun
   Jua kali means hot sun, from workers who work outdoors.

25. A — Giving correct change
   Honesty is right in business.

26. D — One that people want, is safe and can earn more than it costs
   Viable means it can work.

27. C — So that money can be checked and accounted for
   Records show that money was handled honestly.

28. C — Putting litter in the bin
   Using bins keeps the school clean.

29. D — Practise it every day
   Habits grow with practice.

30. D — Doing your class duty without being reminded
   Responsible pupils do their duties.

31. C — So that it runs well and everyone knows what to do
   Planning helps activities succeed.

32. B — Making posters and songs on child protection
   Awareness helps protect children.

33. D — The child helpline 116
   Childline Kenya can be reached on 116.

34. A — Amina
   12 is more than 10.

35. D — Each person has one vote of equal value
   Everyone's vote counts the same.

36. D — Opening prayer or song
   Meetings begin with an opening.

37. C — A teacher patron
   A teacher adviser guides the pupils.

38. A — Assistant chief
   An assistant chief leads a sub-location.

39. B — Welcome visitors and help settle small quarrels
   Village elders help the village.

40. D — The President
   The President leads the national government.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Only teachers decide on discipline, pupil leaders may be unfair, and serious problems must be reported to teachers.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Draw the county outline. Draw the sub-county boundaries. Write the names of the sub-counties. Show the neighbouring counties around the edge. Add a north arrow, a title and a key, then colour it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It asks pupils to study well and treat others with kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for showing action.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give jobs, they buy farmers' produce, and they pay taxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports and games, and festivals and ceremonies.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, 1 mark for two or three.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: The patron is a teacher who guides and advises the pupil leaders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a teacher, 1 mark for guides the pupil leaders.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: A good citizen in school follows the rules, respects others and does what is good for the whole school community.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rules/respect, 1 mark for the community idea.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Landforms: mountain and valley (or hill, plain, plateau). Water features: lake and river (or waterfall, ocean).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: North-east (between north and east), south-east (between south and east), south-west (between south and west), north-west (between north and west).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct in-between point with its place.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the county boundary. Decide how many people one dot stands for. Put more dots where more people live and fewer dots where few live. Add a title and key.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: To know whether there is profit or loss, to show honesty, and to plan better next time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lead the county executive, present the budget and plans, and represent the county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: County A is larger by 6 squares.
   Working / marking points: 15 - 9 = 6. 1 mark for choosing A, 1 mark for subtracting, 1 mark for 6 squares.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: A peace garden where pupils can sit calmly and a peace poster competition to teach about peace. Explain how each helps.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity and 1 mark for each explanation.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ask an adult before going online, do not share private information, and be kind and never bully online.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Write a polite invitation, state the topic, give the date and time, and thank the visitor after the talk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: North, east, south and west.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct points, 2 marks for all four.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: They have the same rights as other children. They may be laughed at or neglected. Including them helps them to learn and be happy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: It gives water for rivers and it attracts tourists. Accept rich soils for farming.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.
